column1: The value for the policy rule parameter in (11.10) can also be interpreted in terms of a signal extraction problem faced by the policy authority. Recall that the basic assumption in the Poole analysis was that the policymaker could observe and react to the interest rate, but perhaps because of information lags, the current values of output and the underlying disturbances could not be observed. Suppose instead that the shocks u, v, and e are observed, and the central bank can respond to them. That is, suppose the policy rule could take the form bt = muut + mvvt + moot for some parameters mu, mv, and mo. If this policy rule is substituted into (11.1) and (11.2), one obtains yt = (c + h + amu)ut - a(1 - mv)vt + a(1 + mo)ot / (a + c + h): In this case, which corresponds to a situation of perfect information about the basic shocks, it is clear that the variance of output can be minimized if mu = (c + h)/a, mv = 1 and mo = 1.
